summary.what_changed: Fixed all remaining broken citation_exists checks across the published docs site (29 pages audited, 3 failing pages / 6 bad citations found and corrected to 0 failing). The fixes covered three categories: two pages had stale intra-repo paths pointing at docs/ instead of the actual docs/site-src/ location; one scoring-criteria row contained an illustrative example path (`.github/workflows/claude.yml` "or similar") that was rewritten as prose instead of being added to the citation-exemption list; and references to three ship-skill spoke files that actually live in the private theoju/claude-config repo were rewritten as plain spoke names rather than path-shaped tokens, avoiding both 404s and disclosure of a private repo's existence/layout on the public site.
summary.why: citation_exists is a Tier-1 block in the docs-agent lint, so any page carrying a bad citation silently fails the first PR that touches it and freezes the docs baseline. This is a follow-up to PR #254 addressing the same latent-trap class across the rest of the site.

doc_targets.notes: Records the site-wide citation_exists sweep (29 pages, 3 fixed) and the three failure patterns found (stale intra-repo paths, illustrative example paths, private-repo spoke references) so future contributors recognize the same trap class before it freezes the docs baseline again.

summary.what_changed: Updated the existing docs-agent baseline-freeze incident retrospective (docs/superpowers/2026-09-14-docs-agent-baseline-freeze-incident.md) to reflect that the incident is actually resolved. Three edits: the status line now shows 'resolved' plus the current baseline (advanced to 2026-09-22T12:31, the first promotion since 08-22, after nightly run #280 auto-merged); a new 'Resolution (2026-09-21)' section separates what held up the freeze (a deadlock reproducible on a sibling host) from what remains unexplained (deferral-counter divergence between the run branch and main on this repo, and zero increments on the dogfood host); and the old 'Recommended next steps' section is kept verbatim but marked superseded. A second commit also corrects an earlier misreading of a `#221: 1` counter entry as a stale fossil — log evidence from run #280 shows PR #221 (merged 2026-08-14) was in fact the live blocker for the full 31.2-day freeze; the wrong sentence is left in place under a correction marker rather than rewritten.
summary.why: The shipped fixes (CCE-175/#274 keying the skip-hatch off last_successful_run.completed_at instead of a merge-only counter; CCE-178/#276 fixing two defects the first production firing exposed; CCE-179/#277 capturing both lessons in the plugin's CLAUDE.md, all merged 2026-09-21) made the incident doc's open-incident framing and its recommended measurement stale and potentially misleading to future readers relying on it as a durable record.

summary.what_changed: Restructured the project README as the GitHub landing page (new section order: what it measures, quick start, daily use, optional setup, how it works, project layout, FAQ, attribution, license), embedded both archify diagrams (architecture and scoring data flow) as light/dark SVG picture previews linking to the live docs site, corrected several stale claims (all 12 dimensions now have Execution scorers, probe catalog has 50 entries, per-axis scoring, real clone URL, 87 vs 75 tip-count explanation), fixed an inaccurate launchd wake claim in README/ROUTINE.md/install.sh (StartCalendarInterval jobs run on next wake, they don't wake the Mac), added a new script (diagram-previews.mjs) that regenerates the SVG previews with a CI drift test, and removed the full MIT license text from the README in favor of a link to LICENSE.
